title: The real marvel
hookLine: Ananda lists the marvels of the birth; the Buddha: here is a marvel, feelings known as they arise

cards: The snowstorm, the taxi, the doctor who almost didn't make it. Some families tell a birth story so often it becomes a kind of legend.
In the hundred and twenty-third discourse, monks are sitting together marveling at the Buddha's powers.
The Buddha asks Ananda to tell them about the wonderful qualities of a Buddha, and Ananda, who heard them from the Buddha's own mouth, starts to recite the marvels of his birth. It's a long list.
And at the very end, the Buddha adds one of his own.

teach.b: Ananda's marvels are the great birth story, as this discourse tells it.
The one who would become the Buddha passes mindfully from a heavenly realm into his mother's womb, and a great light fills the world, even the dark spaces between worlds. Four young gods guard him.
His mother keeps the precepts easily, and can see him within her, the text says, like a thread through a clear gem. She gives birth standing. Gods receive him first.
Two streams of water, one cool and one warm, pour from the sky to bathe them.
He stands at once, takes seven steps, looks in every direction and declares that this is his last birth. And his mother, the text says, dies seven days later.
Each marvel ends: this too I remember as a wonderful quality of the Blessed One. Then the Buddha speaks.
Remember this too, Ananda: for the Buddha, feelings are known as they arise, known as they stay, known as they pass. Perceptions too. Thoughts too.
After the light across the worlds and the seven steps, he points to something almost ordinary: knowing a feeling as it comes and goes. It's the same skill we met with Sariputta, one by one.
The birth wonders happen once, to one being. This one can be practiced on an ordinary afternoon.

how: Buddhists celebrate the birth of the Buddha at Vesak or, in East Asia, on the Buddha's birthday, often by pouring water over a small statue of the infant Buddha standing with one hand raised, recalling the streams of water in the birth story.

o: a gift given to a teacher out of awe
a miracle performed to win followers

p: then he declares his last birth
feelings known as they arise and pass

s: in MN 123 the Buddha adds a final marvel to Ananda's list
feelings, perceptions and thoughts known as they arise, stay and pass.
Ananda says he made up the birth marvels himself
he says he heard and learned them from the Buddha's own mouth.
the text says the Buddha's mother died seven days after his birth
it's one of the marvels Ananda recites.

games.q: Ananda has recited every marvel of the birth: light, gods, seven steps. what does the Buddha add?
o: a marvel of his great powers.
feelings, perceptions and thoughts known as they arise and pass.
games.why: the last marvel is a practice: knowing experience clearly as it comes and goes.

practice: Wait for a feeling, not an emotion story, just the tone: pleasant, unpleasant or neither, an itch, a warm hand, a dull ache. When one appears, know it as it starts, while it stays, and as it fades, then wait for the next.
It's small, and that's the point.

wordCard.voice: Acchariya. Wonderful, a marvel: after Ananda's birth wonders, the Buddha names one more, feelings, perceptions and thoughts, known as they arise, stay and pass.

orig.note: Pali acchariya: wonderful, a marvel. the discourse's title pairs it with abbhuta, astonishing.

carryVoice: Your line: catch it as it begins. The smallest marvel is the one you can practice. Day four ninety-two, done.

sources.ref: Majjhima Nikaya 123, Acchariya-abbhuta Sutta (wonderful and marvelous)
